note: Names, descriptions and grades are the official list as shown by Exophase; rarity percentages and progress counters are PSNProfiles as of 2026-11-19 (the game is not out yet, so most percentages sit at 0.1%). Hidden flags follow the 27 visible / 28 hidden split published by OutputLag. Every guide is written in our own words; a specific place or step is only given when a source below pins it down, and anything else is labelled as our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game. No guide text is copied from any other guide, wiki or forum.

trophies.guide: The platinum pops the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned — there is nothing extra to do for it. Work the roadmap in order: story first, then the side-story finales, then the long grinds (stunts, challenges, collectibles) last, because most of the grind fills itself in while you play. Published estimates put the whole list at around 200 hours; treat that as a rough guide, not a promise. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Unmissable: finish Gone Fishing, the opening mission, and this pops. It is the first story trophy and the most-earned one on the list, so if you are playing the story at all you already have it. Nothing to prepare and no way to miss it. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Unmissable: play through Chapter 1 to its end. Chapter trophies can pop as the next chapter begins rather than on the last cutscene, so do not worry if it does not fire the instant the final mission ends. Before you leave Chapter 1, do the one thing in it that may not come back: Lucia's balcony meditation, which counts toward Positive Mental Attitude (see that trophy). Keep a manual save at the start of every chapter — the game has no mission replay. The chapter-save and balcony details come from OutputLag; the rest is our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Unmissable: finish Chapter 2. This is the chapter where switching between Jason and Lucia opens up (right after Breakfast Run) and most of the list starts to unlock, so use the chapter to open the systems the grind trophies need: the Scooter Bros app, the Real Estate app and the gym. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the switching detail comes from OutputLag.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Unmissable: finish Chapter 3. Do the time-sensitive Race Against Yago in Yago's street-racing strand the moment it appears (it carries an hourglass icon) — the strand counts toward Strangers & Freaks, and a missed timed race is the one story-adjacent thing that can cost you a clean run. Save first, then race. The Yago detail comes from OutputLag; the rest is our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Unmissable: finish Chapter 4. Near the end of this chapter the optional mission That's Where The Money Is opens bank-vault robberies, which feed Maximum Withdrawal, Hot Together and A Classic Blitz Play — do it as soon as it shows up rather than leaving it for the post-game. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the vault-mission detail comes from OutputLag.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Unmissable gold: finish the final mission (the end of Chapter 5). Keep an untouched manual save from just before the final mission — with no mission replay and no New Game Plus, that save is your only way back to the endgame if you want to re-run the finale. After the credits, everything outside the story stays available, so this is a checkpoint, not a finish line. The save advice comes from OutputLag; the rest is our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Unmissable: finish the Breakfast Run mission. It matters beyond its own pop — switching between Jason and Lucia opens right after it, and the partner system it unlocks is what Hot Together, Retail Therapy and Personal Best all need. Play it as the story presents it; there is no alternate route to take. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the switching detail comes from OutputLag.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Unmissable: finish The Cartel Heist mission when the story brings it to you. It is a story beat, not a free-roam robbery — the bank-vault grind trophy (Maximum Withdrawal) is a separate thing that opens later, so do not confuse the two. Just play the mission through. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Unmissable: finish the Child's Play mission. Like the other named-mission trophies it pops from story progress alone, so there is no preparation and no miss window. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Unmissable: finish the Headliners mission. A pure story pop — play the mission when it arrives and move on. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Unmissable: finish the VCIA Takedown mission at Vice City International Airport. Do not confuse it with Catch Me If You Can, the free-roam trophy for stealing a jet from the same airport — that one you do on your own time, this one the story hands you. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Unmissable: finish the Operation Savage Glory mission. Story progress only — no side requirement, no miss window. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Gold for reaching 100% completion — the hardest trophy on the list and the last one most players will earn. The checklist itself only appears after the story, under Progress, Stats, 100% Completion, but work done earlier still counts, so do not wait for it to appear before starting the grind. The checklist asks for more than the individual trophies do: 300 stunts (not 250), 70 of the 80 challenges, 200 of the 277 vehicle models and all 8 bank vaults. Finish the story, the side finales and the collectibles first, then use the checklist as your cleanup list. The checklist thresholds come from OutputLag; the rest is our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Silver for 250 stunts: stunt jumps, under-the-bridge flights, knife flights and base jumps all count. Do not stop at 250 if you want the platinum — 100% completion needs 300. Fold stunts into normal driving rather than grinding them in one sitting: take jumps and bridges whenever a route passes one, and keep a stunt-friendly vehicle handy. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the stunt types and the 300-for-100% figure come from OutputLag.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try all 9 activity types once — one session of each is enough, no wins or medals needed. The fastest way is a sampler run early on: as each activity unlocks, do one round of it before moving on, and tick it off here. The 9 types are the game's activity roster (races, fishing, shooting range, arcade, bowling, meditation, hunting, drone races and gym work are the ones the other trophies name). Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Silver for gold medals in all 42 Shooting Range challenges, spread across two shooting ranges. Gold every challenge at one range before moving to the next, and retry a failed challenge at once while the target layout is fresh in your head. Use the weapon the challenge gives you rather than fighting it with a favourite, and practise the slow, aimed shots first — speed comes after accuracy. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the two-range, 42-challenge split comes from OutputLag.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations — one win per location, not one win total. Learn each course's line on a practice run first: drone races punish missed gates more than slow flying, so fly clean before you fly fast. Tick locations off here as you win them so you can see which ones are left. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the 14-location count comes from OutputLag and PSNProfiles.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different events, not the same race 20 times. Work through the race roster systematically and note which events you have won; street races, and the Yago strand races that count toward Strangers & Freaks, all feed this. Keep a fast, well-handling car tuned for racing rather than switching vehicles every event. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge — a head-to-head fishing contest, not free fishing. Fish a few casual sessions first to learn the casting and reeling timing, then take Cal on when you are comfortable; the challenge is about technique, not gear. If you lose, you can try again. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Finish any one arcade game — any of the four in-game arcade games counts, so pick the one you are best at rather than the first one you find. Completing means seeing it through to its end, not just starting it, so set aside a few uninterrupted minutes. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the four-games detail comes from OutputLag.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's mission strand through to its final mission. Side-story finales stay open after the credits, so there is no rush and no miss window — pick the strand up when it appears and follow it to its end. Note that Andy's strand does not count toward Strangers & Freaks, which has its own 8 strands. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the post-story and non-counting details come from OutputLag.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's mission strand through to its final mission. Like the other side-story finales it stays open after the credits, so work it at your own pace and do not worry about chapter deadlines. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's mission strand through to its final mission. Billy's strand does not count toward Strangers & Freaks, and the finale stays available after the story ends, so there is no miss window — just follow the strand to its conclusion. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the non-counting detail comes from OutputLag.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Silver for finishing 8 stranger mission strands. Not every optional questline counts: Andy's, Billy's and Tyrone's strands have their own trophies and do not count here, so check this trophy's progress counter after each strand you finish to learn which ones register. One to treat as time-sensitive: the Chapter 3 Race Against Yago in Yago's street-racing strand carries an hourglass icon — save first, then race the moment it appears. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the exclusions and the Yago detail come from OutputLag.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's mission strand through to its final mission. A side-story finale that stays open after the credits, so no deadline applies. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's mission strand through to its final mission. Tyrone's strand does not count toward Strangers & Freaks, and the finale stays available after the story, so play it when it appears and follow it to the end. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the non-counting detail comes from OutputLag.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: THE ONE POSSIBLY MISSABLE TROPHY. Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida. Two things make it risky: Lucia's balcony meditation in Chapter 1 disappears once that chapter ends, and there is no mission replay. Do it the morning after the mission Down to Earth, when Lucia heads to the balcony of Jason's house — follow her and accept the optional task — and keep a manual save from the start of Chapter 1 until the trophy pops. Meditation spots show as purple icons when you are close; each outdoor spot should count twice if you meditate there with both characters, so bring your partner every time. The balcony, save and purple-icon details come from OutputLag; it is not confirmed that the trophy strictly needs the balcony spot, so do it anyway. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret Vogel — a Jason-only hunting questline that sends you after animals through target decks. A clean head or heart shot keeps the carcass pristine, so take the shot only when you have a clear line and the animal is still. Follow Bret's strand as it appears; it is a side questline, not a one-off hunt. The Jason-only, target-deck and clean-shot details come from OutputLag; the rest is our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Silver for completing 3 collectible card sets. Pick up cards as you explore rather than hunting them in one late grind — they are scattered across Leonida, and a set completes when you hold every card in it. Track which sets are one card short and prioritise those areas when you travel. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: Silver for using WAiNK It at 100 locations. Make it a habit, not a grind: WAiNK It at every landmark, viewpoint and interesting spot you pass, and the count climbs on its own. Since WAiNK also scans vehicles for Whip It Good, pair the two — scan the traffic around you whenever you stop to WAiNK a location. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the WAiNK-scans-vehicles detail comes from OutputLag.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Finish 50 challenges — the game lists them under Progress, then Challenges, and many complete on their own while you play. Check the list regularly and chase the nearly-done ones first; the easy wins stack up fast. Note the gap for the platinum: 100% completion needs 70 of the 80 challenges, so 50 is a milestone, not the end. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the challenge list location and the 70-of-80 figure come from OutputLag.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level, then lose the cops and get clear of the red heat zone — the trophy pops once you have left the heat zone, not just the flashing search area. The easiest setup is a bank-vault robbery, which gives you 4 stars straight away; escaping one with your partner also earns this. Bring your partner, commit a loud crime, then drive somewhere quiet and wait it out. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the vault and heat-zone details come from OutputLag.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops in a row while the police are still chasing you — if the stars fade and you are only in the red heat zone, the chain breaks. Call your partner first, then hit three shops close together in quick succession and do not stop to fight the cops between them. Give it a moment after the third shop: the trophy can take about 30 seconds to pop. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the chain-break and 30-second details come from OutputLag.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Scanning a vehicle with the WAiNK app counts as discovering it, so scan traffic as you drive instead of trying to steal or drive every model. Park near busy roads and scan what passes, and keep scanning new models you have not seen before — the counter tracks distinct models. 100% completion needs 200 of the 277 base models, so keep the habit going past this trophy. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the WAiNK-scan and 200-of-277 details come from OutputLag.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Down 5 enemies in one use of Combat Focus, the slow-motion aim you trigger by pressing L3 and R3 while aiming. Pick a group of enemies standing close together — the guards at an illegal operation are a good target — and use an assault rifle. Adrenaline extends Focus, so pop it before you start. Line the group up first, then trigger Focus and work across them without letting it drop. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the button, weapon and Adrenaline details come from OutputLag.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Steal a large passenger plane from Vice City International Airport and take off without a schedule. Only planes docked at a boarding bridge count — planes parked elsewhere on the airfield do not — and the planes at gates E3 and E4 work. Get to the cockpit, back out toward the runway and take off, then fly about 1 km away from the airport; the trophy is delayed and pops once you are clear. Save first, because the police come fast. The gates and 1 km details come from OutputLag; the rest is our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: Get into a Rhino military tank — 'Kinda hot in these Rhinos' is the game's wink at it. Tanks should be parked on the south side of Mile Zero Air Station, on the island at the far southwest of the map. Save first, get in, then drive and fire until the trophy pops. Expect a heavy police response, so do not plan anything delicate right after. The Mile Zero detail comes from OutputLag; the rest is our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being seen. First unlock the tool: the Chapter 3 mission Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs gives you the Snap Gun and opens jewelry-store robberies. Go to a store's locked back door and use the Snap Gun on it — kicking the door in sets off the alarm. Inside the back room, find the note with the safe code, open the safe, and leave without being seen. Richardson Jewelry & Diamonds in Vice City is a good target. If someone spots you, reload rather than pushing on. The Snap Gun, safe-code and store details come from OutputLag; the rest is our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Silver for robbing 5 bank vaults and escaping. Vaults unlock through That's Where The Money Is, an optional mission near the end of Chapter 4: tail an armored security van to a large bank and get into the vault while the guard has it open. You cannot carry all the bags alone, so bring your partner — and escaping with your partner also earns Hot Together, since a vault job gives you 4 stars straight away. 100% completion needs all 8 vaults, so keep going past 5. The mission and partner details come from OutputLag; the rest is our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape — then get clear of the red heat zone, because like the other escape trophies this one only pops once you have left the heat zone, not just the flashing search area. Ambush a truck on a quiet stretch of road, grab the cash, and drive somewhere the cops cannot follow before you slow down. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the heat-zone detail comes from OutputLag.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida. This fills in naturally as you travel for missions, strands and collectibles — the trick is not to fast-travel everywhere and skip the map. When the counter stalls, look for the blank patches on your map and drive through them deliberately; the last few areas are usually small pockets you never had a reason to visit. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. Work gang by gang and tick each one off here — the trophy pops when the ninth gang's operation is done. 100% completion wants all 39 operations, so this trophy pops along the way to that bigger count. Illegal operations also make good Gunslinger practice, since their guards stand in groups. The 9-gang and 39-operation figures come from OutputLag; the rest is our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Go to a bar or beachfront spot on Ocean Beach, order a cocktail, and take it in where you can see the water — the trophy is about the moment, not a mission, so slow down and let the scene play. If it does not pop at the first bar, try another beachfront spot. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — drive a car straight through the showroom glass, the way the old games taught you. Pick a showroom with a big front window, build a little speed inside, and go through it rather than out the door. Save first in case the stunt goes wrong or the cops arrive mid-smash. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — Kingpin Bowling, an illegal operation you visit in Chapter 2. Bring Sticky Bombs. Take all three key valuables: the luxury watch in an office, the shotgun on a table, and the contents of the office safe, which you blow open with a Sticky Bomb. Then escape the police. If you leave something behind, the operation comes back later, so it is not missable. The Kingpin Bowling and valuables details come from OutputLag; the rest is our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: A partnership with mass appeal — it should pop when Jason and Lucia both reach maximum Strength. Buy a gym membership and train with your partner there, since the partner trains alongside you. Work on both characters' Strength steadily rather than maxing one and forgetting the other. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the maximum-Strength reading comes from OutputLag.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Perform 500 actions that change your Criminal Profile. Robberies and fights feed it, so it fills up without a separate grind if you play the game the way it wants to be played — rob shops, vaults and operations, and get into fights along the way. Check the counter under Progress to see how far along you are. The 500-action reading comes from OutputLag; the rest is our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: The official description is deliberately cryptic: 'Second time's the charm.' No source pins down the exact trigger yet — it reads like a second-chance event, something that only fires after a first failure. The honest advice is to keep playing and watch for a moment where the game gives you another shot at something; do not chase it until a checked method appears. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the unverified status is confirmed by OutputLag.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: Another cryptic one: 'What the hell just happened?' It points to a strange, hidden encounter somewhere in Leonida — the kind of thing you stumble into while exploring, not something on a checklist. Explore odd corners of the map, especially at night, and pay attention to anything out of the ordinary. Until a checked trigger is published, treat this as an exploration trophy. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game; the unverified status is confirmed by OutputLag.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by — a melee attack from a moving vehicle. Drive slowly past a pedestrian, swing a melee weapon as you pass, and keep moving. It is a deliberately silly stunt, so pick a quiet street, save first, and try it a few times until the hit connects. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts — the total is cumulative. Marked bills come from bank and payday-loan jobs, and you launder them by selling them to your contacts, so every vault and payday job feeds this counter. Do not spend marked bills directly; route them through a contact every time and the total climbs on its own. The marked-bill source and laundering route come from OutputLag; the rest is our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — cumulative, and every kind of shop counts. You will get most of the way there just by buying weapons, ammo, clothes and car upgrades as you play. If you are short near the end, top up with big-ticket purchases you actually want (a good car, weapon upgrades) rather than throwing money away on things you will never use. Our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Buy all 8 garage properties in the Vice City Real Estate app, which unlocks after the Chapter 2 mission Daily Driver. Together they cost about $160,000, and garages the story gives you do not count — only bought ones do. Save up and buy them in a batch once the app is open, and remember each registered car needs a free garage space (see On the Spot). The 8-garage, $160,000 and app details come from OutputLag; the rest is our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The Chapter 2 mission Moses opens the app: take a stolen car to Moses, choose Respray, then Register. From Chapter 3 you can also register cars with a standard tracker at Pay 'n' Spray. Each car needs a free garage space, so buy garages first (see Little Boxes) and register cheap, common cars — there is no benefit to registering rare ones. The Moses and Pay 'n' Spray details come from OutputLag; the rest is our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.
trophies.name: On the Spot
